$comment_minimumCacheTTL: SAFE BECAUSE THE CACHE KEY IS THE SOURCE URL, AND BOTH MEDIA HOSTS
MINT A NEW URL WHEN THE UNDERLYING PHOTO CHANGES:
R2       — object keys embed an epoch-ms mint stamp, e.g.
Cotality — the MediaURL path embeds a Unix timestamp; the segment
So a replaced or re-synced photo produces a DIFFERENT optimizer
cache key. A stale transform is therefore unreachable rather than
served — no listing update can be masked by this TTL, and no purge
step is required. A short TTL would only re-transform identical
bytes under a new cache-write charge.
The listing-media freshness contract is unaffected: the DTO decides
WHICH url a card renders, and that decision is not cached here.
$comment_otherRemoteHosts: Non-listing image hosts required by marketing pages. Listed here so

The card helper does NOT trust these.
